claims.claim: Teghaza 001 formed more than 4.1 billion years ago and matches mineralogy at 13 highland sites on Mars.
claims.episode_span: A 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite offers the oldest direct sample of the red planet's crust and mantle.
claims.source_title: Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
claims.supporting_quote: This global map of Mars shows 13 locations that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth.

claims.claim: Copernicus Sentinel-3 captured Super Typhoon Champi on 21 October 2026 with an eye spanning approximately 50 km.
claims.episode_span: Copernicus Sentinel-3 captured the storm on 21 October 2026 off Taiwan and the Philippines. The false-colour image assigns green, white and light grey to the coldest cloud tops at -70 °C.
claims.source_title: Earth from Space: Champi’s eerie eye
claims.supporting_quote: This image of Super Typhoon Champi from Copernicus Sentinel-3 was captured on 21 October 2026 off the coasts of Taiwan and the Philippines.

claims.claim: Most asteroid mass near white dwarfs stays in 0.1-to-1 km fragments because of van der Waals forces between grains.
claims.episode_span: New modelling shows rubble-pile asteroids retain internal strength from van der Waals forces between grains. Most mass stays in 0.1-to-1 km pieces rather than turning directly to dust.
claims.source_title: Asteroids venturing near white dwarfs don't break directly into dust, study reveals
claims.supporting_quote: When asteroids travel too close to white dwarfs, the dense remnants of stars that have exhausted their nuclear fuel, powerful gravitational forces can tear them apart. However, new research from Planetary Science Institute (PSI) suggests that these asteroids don't immediately break into dust.
